prf:wedderburn-mass-formula:
Proof Proof of wedderburn mass formula. Work over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] at generic q, passing to the fraction field where inverses are required; write h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} for the Hecke parameter and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) for the Markov weight, so that the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is the linear functional normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z (positive stabilisation).

Step 1 — extremal Wedderburn blocks and channel eigenvalues. By the three-parameter decomposition, H_3(R, q) \cong M_1(R) \oplus M_2(R) \oplus M_1(R), with blocks labelled by the partitions (3), (2,1), (1,1,1); for general n the corresponding extremal blocks are the symmetric [n], standard [n-1, 1], and alternating [1^n] representations. The Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 gives each generator the eigenvalue q in the symmetric channel and -q^{-1} in the alternating channel; since all \sigma_i are conjugate, the two one-dimensional blocks are the algebra characters \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(\sigma_i) = q and \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(\sigma_i) = -q^{-1}. A typed crossing element X = c \cdot \sigma_i + d \cdot \mathbf{1} (transfer matrix) therefore evaluates in the two scalar channels as

\lambda^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X) = cq + d,
\qquad
\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X)
  = -c q^{-1} + d .

Step 2 — the transfer matrix is the regular representation of the crossing algebra. A single crossing generates the two-dimensional commutative algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), in which \sigma^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma + 1. In the ordered basis (\sigma, 1), multiplication by X = c\sigma + d has matrix exactly the crossing (transfer) matrix of the statement,

T(X) =
\begin{pmatrix}
  c h_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\
  c & d
\end{pmatrix},

since X \cdot \sigma = c\sigma^2 + d\sigma = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,\sigma + c and X \cdot 1 = c\sigma + d. As a matrix of left multiplication, T is an algebra homomorphism: T(X)\,T(X') = T(XX'), which one verifies directly — XX' = c''\sigma + d'' with c'' = cc'h_{\mathrm{A}} + cd' + c'd and d'' = cc' + dd', matching the entries of the matrix product. Consequently, for the chained element X_i := \prod_{j > i} X_j of the crossings of all strands j > i, the transfer-matrix chain satisfies M_i = \prod_{j > i} T(X_j) = T(X_i), and reading off the basis coefficients gives (M_i)_{12} = (M_i)_{21} = c_i and (M_i)_{22} = d_i, where X_i = c_i \sigma + d_i. Moreover the eigenvalues of M_i = T(X_i) are precisely the two character values \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i) and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i), since the regular representation of R[\sigma] diagonalises along its two characters. (Chaining within a single crossing algebra is the defining Level-0 transfer-matrix reduction; the exact all-partitions computation replaces it for n \ge 4, as the statement records.)

Step 3 — the three invariants are the three extremal block readouts.

  1. Markov trace (standard block). By linearity and the normalisation above, \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = c_i\,z + d_i = z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}. Hence \Phi_1 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}\bigr\rvert = \sum_i \ln\lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i)\rvert is the Markov-weighted trace datum of the chain — the invariant attached to the standard (dim n{-}1) block in the correspondence table.
  2. Determinant = sym \times alt. Directly, \det T(X) = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,d - c^2 = cdh_{\mathrm{A}} + d^2 - c^2 = (cq + d)(-cq^{-1} + d) = \lambda^{\mathrm{sym}}\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}}; equivalently this is the product of the two eigenvalues exhibited in Step 2. By multiplicativity of the determinant and of the characters, \det M_i = \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\,\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so \Phi_2 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert + \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).
  3. Ratio = sym / alt (chirality). \Phi_3 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert - \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).

From 2 and 3, \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert and \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert are recovered as half the sum and half the difference of the per-chain summands: the pair (\Phi_2, \Phi_3) is an invertible linear repackaging of the two one-dimensional block evaluations, while \Phi_1 carries the standard-block Markov datum. The triple (\Phi_1, \Phi_2, \Phi_3) therefore carries exactly the evaluations of the three extremal Wedderburn blocks on the chain — no more and no fewer. This is the claimed completeness at the 2 \times 2 transfer level: the chain data (c_i, d_i) \in R^2 of the two-dimensional crossing algebra support precisely the two characters and the Markov functional exhibited, and every block-respecting multiplicative invariant of \{M_i\} is a function of these three. For n \ge 4 the non-extremal partitions contribute additional invariants, computed exactly by the full partition sum via Young's seminormal form, as stated.

Step 4 — the coefficients. The overall scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the archimedean evaluation of the algebraic binding scale m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_3), with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G the Borromean volume (binding scale). The determinant weight \beta_2 = -2[3]_q has a direct count: the three color channels give the pair count \binom{3}{2} = 3, q-deformed to [3]_q, with the sign fixed by the determinant sign accumulation and the factor 2 by the \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} crossing-doubling convention established there. The chirality weight h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 is the minimal even power of the Hecke parameter compatible with the S-parity classification of the three terms (S-classification) and with the vanishing of the chirality contribution in the commutative limit (commutative chirality): h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 as q \to 1, so h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \to 0 and the classical mass formula retains no chirality term. All three weights are functions of q alone, evaluated at q_0, and the scale is fixed by m_e: no fitted parameter enters.

Assembling: the binding functional \alpha\,(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q\,\Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3) is the weighted sum of the three extremal-block invariants of the atomic braid established in Steps 1–3, with the weights of Step 4, added to the free constituent masses Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z \cdot m_e. \square

The numerical agreement of this formula with measured atomic masses across the nuclide table is an empirical cross-check, not part of the proof.
rem:level-zero-discards-braid-noncommuta:
Remark Level-0 discards braid non-commutativity at every n \geq 3, not only the non-extremal blocks at n \geq 4. The statement records that for n \geq 4 the Hecke algebra carries irreducible representations beyond the three extremal ones, and that the invariants they produce are not captured by the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix. That is a statement about the count of blocks. It is not a statement that the transfer-matrix construction is complete below n = 4, and reading it as one overstates the theorem.

A second approximation is present at every n \geq 3, independent of the block count. Step 2 of the proof forms the chained element X_i = \prod_{j > i} X_j inside the two-dimensional crossing algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), which is commutative, and sets M_i = T(X_i). The crossings so chained belong to different strand pairs, and the corresponding braid generators do not commute in H_n(q) for any n \geq 3. The Level-0 reduction therefore discards braid non-commutativity as well as the non-extremal blocks, and only the second of those is an n \geq 4 effect.

The two are easy to conflate because the dimensions agree at n = 3: the standard block of H_3(q) has dimension n - 1 = 2, and so does R[\sigma]. This is a coincidence of dimension, not an identification. By Step 2 the two eigenvalues of M_i are the symmetric and alternating characters \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so the standard representation does not act on M_i at all; the row labelled standard in the correspondence table records the Markov functional \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = z \, (M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22} on the crossing algebra, not an image of the two-dimensional block.

Deuterium is the unique atom with n = A + Z = 3. It is therefore both the smallest atom carrying two distinct braid generators and the only one at which the extremal blocks exhaust the partitions, which makes it the single point at which the two approximations can be separated. Evaluating the functional there gives

  \alpha\bigl(
    \Phi_1 - 2[3]_q \cdot \Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3
  \bigr)
  \approx -6.214 \; \mathrm{MeV},

against a measured -B(\mathrm{D}) \approx -2.225 \; \mathrm{MeV}. Since no non-extremal block exists at n = 3, the discrepancy is attributable to the Level-0 reduction alone. It bounds the magnitude of that one approximation and excludes no ingredient of the construction. The evaluation, together with checks of the Step 2 readouts and of the commutativity of R[\sigma] against the non-commutativity of H_3(q), has been carried out exactly.

prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form:
Proposition Hoefsmit seminormal matrices as R-matrix evaluations in H_n(q). For each partition \lambda \vdash n and aether parameter q > 1, the Hoefsmit seminormal form [hoefsmit1974] gives an explicit matrix representation \rho_\lambda\colon H_n(R, q) \to M_{d_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}) where d_\lambda = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)| is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda. The generator \sigma_i acts on the basis of standard tableaux by:

  \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i)_{ss'}
  =
  \begin{cases}
    a_\rho & s' = s, \\
    b & s' = s_i, \\
    0 & \text{otherwise},
  \end{cases}

where s_i is the tableau obtained by swapping entries i and i+1 in s (if the result is a valid standard tableau), and the matrix entries are:

  a_\rho = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{1 - q^{-2\rho}},
  \qquad
  b = \sqrt{a_\rho \cdot a_{-\rho} + 1},

with \rho = c(s, i{+}1) - c(s, i) the axial distance (content difference) between the cells containing i{+}1 and i in tableau s.

These matrices satisfy the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i + 1 and the braid relation \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}, and are the explicit R-matrix evaluations that dictate topological crossings in braid and knot diagrams.
prf:hoefsmit-seminormal-form:
Proof Proof of hoefsmit seminormal form. The classical Young seminormal form (Young [young1901], Rutherford [rutherford1948]) represents the symmetric group S_n on the basis of standard Young tableaux with diagonal entry 1/\rho for the transposition (i, i{+}1), where \rho is the axial distance. Hoefsmit [hoefsmit1974] and independently Wenzl [wenzl1988] showed that the q-deformation replaces 1/\rho with

  a_\rho = \frac{h}{1 - q^{-2\rho}},
  \quad h = q - q^{-1},

which at q = 1 (where h \to 0, q^{-2\rho} \to 1) recovers a_\rho \to 1/\rho by l'H^{o}pital's rule.

The Hecke relation follows from the 2 \times 2 block structure: for a pair of tableaux (s, s_i) related by swapping i \leftrightarrow i{+}1, the block

  \begin{pmatrix} a_\rho & b \\ b & a_{-\rho} \end{pmatrix}

has eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} (the two eigenvalues of \sigma_i), and determinant a_\rho \cdot a_{-\rho} - b^2 = -1. The off-diagonal b^2 = a_\rho \cdot a_{-\rho} + 1 ensures \det = -1, which is equivalent to the Hecke relation.

When the swap s_i is not a valid standard tableau, the entry is 1 \times 1 with value a_\rho = q (if i and i{+}1 are in the same row) or a_\rho = -q^{-1} (same column).

Connection to the R-matrix. In the quantum group U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), the universal R-matrix \mathcal{R} \in U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)^{\otimes 2} acts on the tensor product V_\lambda \otimes V_\mu of irreducible representations. The Hoefsmit matrix \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i) is the evaluation of \check{R} = P \circ \mathcal{R} (the braiding map) on the i-th and (i{+}1)-th tensor factors in the n-fold tensor product V^{\otimes n}, restricted to the isotypic component of type \lambda.

This identification is what allows the Hecke algebra trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho_\lambda(\beta)) to compute the Jones polynomial J_K(q) = \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot \chi_\lambda(\beta) / d_\lambda, where \beta is the braid whose closure is the knot K.

Application to figure-eight BW coefficients. The trace \chi_{4_1}([2{,}1]) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho_{[2,1]}(\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1} \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2)) = 2 - [3]_q is computed by multiplying four 2 \times 2 Hoefsmit matrices in the standard representation of H_3(R, q). The result 2 - [3]_q = -1 - h^2 lands on a q-integer expression because each matrix entry is a rational function of q, and the trace is a Laurent polynomial in q. \square
prop:figure-eight-branching-rule:
Proposition Figure-eight character from Young's lattice branching multiplicities. For any partition \lambda \vdash k and aether parameter q > 1, the Frobenius character of the figure-eight braid 4_1 = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1 in the irreducible representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) is determined by three branching multiplicities in Young's lattice:

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = \bigl(f^{\lambda/[3]} + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} - f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}\bigr)
  \;-\; f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot h^2

where f^{\lambda/\mu} = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda/\mu)| is the number of standard Young tableaux of skew shape \lambda/\mu (equivalently, the number of saturated chains from \mu to \lambda in Young's lattice), and h = q - q^{-1}.

The two components are:

  • a_\lambda = f^{\lambda/[3]} + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} - f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}: the classical part (the S_k character of the 3-cycle (123) embedded in S_k).
  • b_\lambda = -f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]}: the q-deformation correction, always \leq 0.

Verified to machine precision (< 10^{-12}) against explicit Hoefsmit seminormal matrix computation for all 191 partitions at k = 3 through k = 11.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.

Proof Proof of figure eight branching rule. The figure-eight braid 4_1 lives in H_3(R, q) (three strands). Its character in an irreducible representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) with k \geq 3 factors through the restriction H_k(R, q) \downarrow H_3(R, q):

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = \sum_{\mu \,\vdash\, 3} f^{\lambda/\mu} \cdot \chi(4_1, \mu)

where f^{\lambda/\mu} is the branching multiplicity --- the number of standard Young tableaux of skew shape \lambda/\mu, counting the distinct ways to remove k - 3 cells from \lambda along a saturated chain in Young's lattice to arrive at \mu.

The three partitions of 3 contribute:

See Table 1.

Substituting:

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = f^{\lambda/[3]} \cdot 1
  + f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot (-1 - h^2)
  + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} \cdot 1

Collecting the constant and h^2 terms gives the result.

Combinatorial structure of b_\lambda. Since b_\lambda = -f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} is always non-positive, and f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} = 0 if and only if \lambda does not contain the Young diagram of [2{,}1] (i.e. \lambda is a single row [k] or a single column [1^k]), the q-deformation correction vanishes precisely for the trivial and sign representations.

The BW scaling of each partition is determined by:

  1. Content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i): positive \to A-dominated (volume/surface), negative \to Z/N-dominated (Coulomb/exchange), zero \to isospin-sensitive (Wigner/hook).

  2. Self-conjugacy (\lambda = \lambda'): self-conjugate partitions contribute isospin Casimir terms (T(T+1)/A, T(T+1)(T+2)/A^2, etc.).

  3. Conjugate pairing (\{\lambda, \lambda'\} with \lambda \neq \lambda'): the sum \lambda \oplus \lambda' gives charge-symmetric corrections (form factor, pn correlation).

  4. Hook partitions ([k-r, 1^r]): the H_3 \hookrightarrow H_k branching multiplicity determines shell effects via the nuclear magic numbers. \square
sec:mass-algebraic-consolidated-intro:
With the Wedderburn decomposition and the Hoefsmit seminormal basis in place, the mass functional reduces to explicit operator evaluations on braid words. This section develops the three algebraic pillars of that evaluation:

  2. Two-row Markov corrections and the Temperley–Lieb radical: Under the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the three-strand antisymmetriser weight y_{(1^3)} vanishes identically. The radical of the Markov Gram pairing G on H_n(q) coincides with the kernel of the Temperley–Lieb quotient H_n(q) \twoheadrightarrow \mathrm{TL}_n(q), so G descends to a positive-definite sesquilinear form on \mathrm{TL}_n(q) while blocking any naive unquotiented Connes distance.
  3. Bi-filtration and the adelic base ring: The Lusztig bar involution and the Hermitian star involution induce a joint cellular-depth and jet-degree bi-filtration on H_n(q), conjecturally stratified by the curvature rank of the Hecke curvature 2-cocycle, linking the algebraic layer to its archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}.
thm:markov-trace-factorization:
Theorem Exact factorization of the nuclear Markov trace. Let \mathcal{N}(Z, N) be the nuclear braid word in H_A(q), presented with its crossings grouped by generator in increasing order, \mathcal{N} = X_0 X_1 \cdots X_{A-2} with each X_i a product of factors c\,\sigma_i + d at the single generator \sigma_i. At each generator, let (a_i, b_i) be the transfer-matrix-reduced chain coefficients, so X_i = a_i \sigma_i + b_i. Let z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) be the Markov trace parameter. The Markov trace factors exactly:

  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\!\bigl(
    \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=0}^{A-2}
  \bigl(z \cdot a_i + b_i\bigr).

Each factor \hat{V}_i = z \cdot a_i + b_i is a rational function of q (since z = q^3/(q^2+1)), with coefficients in \mathbb{Z}[\tfrac12]. The full trace is their product.

The grouping hypothesis is essential. Letters at adjacent generators do not commute, so a word that interleaves them, such as \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 or the Borromean core (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3, cannot be regrouped into this form, and its trace does not factor: \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1) = h z^2 + z \neq z^3.

The transfer matrix IS the polynomial. At each crossing between nucleons i and j, the transfer matrix

  T_j = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c_j(q - q^{-1}) + d_j & c_j \\
    c_j & d_j
  \end{pmatrix}

carries polynomial entries. The crossing types determine the coefficients:

Pair type c_j d_j \det(T_j)
\mathfrak{p}-\mathfrak{p} 1 0 -1
\mathfrak{n}-\mathfrak{n} 1 -(q - q^{-1}) -1
mixed 1 -\frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) -1 - \frac{1}{4}(q - q^{-1})^2

The product of k_i transfer matrices at generator \sigma_i yields M_i \in \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}(q)), whose entries are polynomials of degree bounded by 2k_i. Then \hat{V}_i(q) = z \cdot (M_i)_{21} + (M_i)_{22} evaluates the Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q) in factored form.

Asymptotic behaviour. For heavy nuclei (A \gg 1), the ratio of L_0^{-} and parent traces converges:

  \frac{\mathrm{tr}(L_0^{-})}{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{N})}
   \;\longrightarrow\;
  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{1 - q^{-1}}
   \;\approx\;  10.09.

The sub-leading O(1/A) correction carries the nucleus-specific shell structure and pairing data.
prf:markov-trace-factorization:
Proof Proof of markov trace factorization. By hypothesis the nuclear braid word is X_0 X_1 \cdots X_{A-2}, where X_i collects the crossing factors at the single generator \sigma_i. Using \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1, each X_i reduces to a_i \sigma_i + b_i. This step needs the grouping: Hecke reduction does not regroup an interleaved word, since adjacent generators do not commute.

The full reduced element is the product \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} (a_i \sigma_i + b_i) where the factors are ordered by generator index (right to left: \sigma_{A-2} first, \sigma_0 last).

The Markov trace processes this product by peeling generators from the right. At each step, \sigma_i is the rightmost (largest) generator in the remaining word, and the Markov property gives:

  \mathrm{tr}(\cdots (a_i \sigma_i + b_i))
  = 
  (z \cdot a_i + b_i) \cdot \mathrm{tr}(\cdots).

This works because:

  1. The chain at \sigma_i reduces to a_i \sigma_i + b_i (a linear combination of \sigma_i and the identity).

  2. The Markov property \mathrm{tr}(x \sigma_n) = z\mathrm{tr}(x) applies to the \sigma_i term, and \mathrm{tr}(x \cdot 1) = \mathrm{tr}(x) for the identity term.

  3. Generator \sigma_i is the rightmost active generator when processing from right to left, so the Markov property applies directly.

  4. The remaining word after peeling \sigma_i involves only generators \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{i-1}, which are independent of \sigma_i.

Applying this recursively from i = A-2 down to i = 0 gives the product formula. \square

prop:skein-polynomial-transfer-matrix:
Proposition The nuclear Skein polynomial as a transfer matrix product in q. The aether parameter q acts as the variable of the nuclear Skein polynomial. The transfer matrix product computes this polynomial in factored form without expansion.

Let \mathcal{N}(Z, N) be a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons. The Markov trace (factorization theorem)

  P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)
   := 
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\!\bigl(
    \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \bigr)
  = 
  \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)

Proposition Beta decay as a universal matrix-valued polynomial in q. Beta decay is mediated by the T_{3,5} torus knot with 10 crossings. The T_{3,5} insertion at the converting quark produces a universal 2\times2 matrix-valued polynomial \Delta_\beta(q) that governs every beta transition in every nucleus. The transfer matrix captures the effect of the 10-crossing weak vertex on each nucleon pair.

The three crossing transfer matrices

Each nucleon pair (i, j) contributes a transfer matrix T(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[\tfrac{1}{2}][q^{\pm 1}]):

  T(c, d) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\

  T_{pp}(q) =  T(1, 0) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  T_{nn}(q) =  T(1, -(q - q^{-1})) = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    0 & 1 \\
    1 & -(q - q^{-1})
  \end{pmatrix}

    \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) & 1 \\[4pt]

  =  T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q) - T_{nn}(q)
  =  T_{pp}(q) - T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q)
  =  \Delta_\beta^{\mathrm{mix} \to pp}(q)

  \boxed{
    \Delta_\beta(q)
    = 
    \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) \mathbb{I}
  }

where \mathbb{I} is the 2 \times 2 identity. The decay matrix is a scalar multiple of the identity — beta decay uniformly scales all channels by \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}).

rem:transfer-matrix-operator-properties:
Remark Action on the GS ideal, operator algebra, interaction catalogue, and composition rules. The transfer matrix T_{K_1, K_2}(q) acts on the Gröbner--Shirshov-reduced Hecke chain, generates a non-commutative operator algebra under composition, and catalogues every particle interaction together with its \Delta operator and composition rules.

Action on the Gröbner--Shirshov ideal

The transfer matrix acts on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra element a\sigma_i + b (the Gröbner--Shirshov-reduced chain at generator \sigma_i) by left multiplication followed by Hecke reduction:

  T_{K_1, K_2}  \cdot  (a\sigma + b)
   := 
  (c\sigma + d)(a\sigma + b)
  \stackrel{T^2 = (q-q^{-1})T + 1}{\longrightarrow}
  a'\sigma + b'

where:

  a' = ac(q - q^{-1}) + ad + bc,
  \qquad
  b' = ac + bd.

In matrix form:

  \begin{pmatrix} a' \\ b' \end{pmatrix}
  = 
  T_{K_1, K_2}(q)
   \cdot 
  \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix}

The product of k transfer matrices at generator \sigma_i gives the full chain reduction M_i = \prod_{j} T_j(q), and the Markov-traced volume is \hat{V}_i = z \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}.

The operator algebra

Transfer matrices compose: if strands K_1, K_2, K_3 cross in sequence at generator \sigma_i, the combined operator is:

  T_{K_1 K_3} \circ T_{K_1 K_2}
  = 
  T_{K_1, K_3}(q) \cdot T_{K_1, K_2}(q)

(matrix multiplication). This is non-commutative — the order of crossings matters.

The Gröbner--Shirshov ideal is the kernel:

  I_i =  \ker\!\left(
    \prod_{j} T_j(q) - M_i(q)
  \right)

The ideal I_i at generator \sigma_i absorbs the terms eliminated by the Hecke relation (T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1). The transfer matrix product M_i(q) is the quotient — the element surviving after modding out I_i.

Interaction catalogue

Every particle interaction corresponds to a transfer matrix. The interaction type is determined by the knot types of the two strands at the crossing:

Nuclear interactions (quark-level, Level 1)

Each quark is an unknot strand of \mathcal{B}_3 (up quark); the strands are distinguished by crossing orientation, not knot type.

Interaction K_1 K_2 T(q) Physical
\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u} unknot, \sigma_i unknot, \sigma_i T_{pp} proton-proton repulsion
\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} T_{nn} neutron-neutron
\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} unknot, \sigma_i unknot, \sigma_i^{-1} T_{\mathrm{mix}} proton-neutron binding

Electromagnetic interactions (electron-level)

Interaction K_1 K_2 Physical
e-\mathfrak{p} T_{2,3} \mathcal{B}_3 Electron-nucleus Coulomb
e-e T_{2,3} T_{2,3} Electron-electron repulsion
\gamma-e \varnothing T_{2,3} Photon absorption/emission

Photon-electron transfer matrix

The photon (\varnothing, empty knot) crossing with the electron (T_{2,3}, trefoil) gives:

  T_{\gamma e}(q)
  = 
  T_{\varnothing, T_{2,3}}(q)

Since the empty knot has J_{\varnothing}(q) = 1: c_{\gamma e} = J_{T_{2,3}}(q) / J_{T_{2,3}}(q) = 1 and d_{\gamma e} = 0. Therefore:

  T_{\gamma e}(q) =  T_{pp}(q)
  = 
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}

The photon-electron transfer matrix is the same as the proton-proton matrix. This is because J_{\varnothing}(q) = 1 (trivial Jones polynomial of the empty knot), so the photon contributes no deformation — the crossing is purely determined by the electron.

Shell transitions as R-I moves

Photon absorption promotes an electron from shell n to shell n+1. In the transfer matrix language, this is a Reidemeister I move on the electron-nucleus Hopf link: a curl is added to the electron trefoil, changing its writhe by \pm 1 but preserving its knot type.

The R-I move at the electron-nucleus junction:

  \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i \cdot \sigma_n

adds one transfer matrix factor T_{\gamma e} to the chain at generator \sigma_i. The energy change is:

  \Delta E_n
  = 
  \hat{V}_i^{(n+1)} - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}
  = 
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{11}
  + (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{21}
  - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}

For hydrogen (A = 1, single electron-proton junction): the transfer matrix at shell n is T_{\gamma e}^n (the n-th power). The energy:

  E_n  \propto  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  = 
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{11} + (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{21}

Since T_{\gamma e} has eigenvalues \lambda_{\pm} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[(q - q^{-1}) \pm \sqrt{(q - q^{-1})^2 + 4}\bigr], the n-th power grows as \lambda_+^n, and the energy scales as:

  E_n  \propto  \lambda_+^n

The energy difference between shells:

  \Delta E_{n \to n+1}
  = 
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^{n+1}) - \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  = 
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n) \cdot (\lambda_+ - 1)

This gives the photon energy for shell transitions — a geometric series in the eigenvalue \lambda_+ of the photon-electron transfer matrix.

Interaction as Δ operator

Any interaction that changes the crossing type from (K_1, K_2) \to (K_1', K_2') is encoded by the interaction operator:

  \Delta_{K_1 K_2 \to K_1' K_2'}(q)
  = 
  T_{K_1', K_2'}(q) - T_{K_1, K_2}(q)

This is a 2\times2 matrix with polynomial entries in q.

Interaction \Delta operator Physical process
\beta^- decay \Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} \mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u} crossing change
\beta^+ decay -\Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{pp} \mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{d} crossing change
Photon absorption \Delta_\gamma = T_{\gamma e} (appended) R-I move adds crossing
Pair creation \Delta_{\mathrm{pair}} = T_{ee} - T_{\gamma\gamma} \gamma \to e^+ e^-

For beta decay, \Delta_\beta is universal (beta decay matrix): the same matrix for every nucleus.

For photon absorption, the operator is not a difference but an extension: a new transfer matrix factor T_{\gamma e} is appended to the chain, increasing the color degree by 1.

Composition rules

Sequential interactions (two interactions in sequence at the same generator):

  \Delta_{\mathrm{total}} = \Delta_2 \cdot T_{\mathrm{between}} \cdot \Delta_1
  + \Delta_1 + \Delta_2

Parallel interactions (interactions at different generators):

  \frac{P_{\mathrm{final}}}{P_{\mathrm{initial}}}
  = 
  \prod_{i \in \mathrm{affected}} \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{final}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{initial}}}

The generators factorize — each affected generator contributes independently to the Skein polynomial ratio.

rem:transfer-matrix-identities-context:
Remark Corollaries: nuclear binding from mixed crossings and scalar pairing.

Corollaries

Nuclear binding from mixed crossings only. Identity (i) means that adjacent pp and nn crossings cancel in the transfer matrix chain. In the interleaved ground-state ordering, pp crossings (from proton-proton pairs) and nn crossings (from neutron-neutron pairs) contribute zero net effect. All nuclear binding energy arises from the mixed (pn) crossings, whose transfer matrix T_{pn} has trace 0 and determinant -(1 + h^2/4).

Scalar pairing from mixed crossings. Identity (ii) means that every pair of mixed crossings produces a scalar (proportional to I). The binding strength per pair is [2]_q^2/4 = (q + q^{-1})^2/4, which is the square of half the quantum 2-integer. At q_0: [2]_q^2/4 \approx 1.011.
prf:transfer-matrix-identities:
Proof Proof of transfer matrix identities. (i) Direct multiplication. With h = q - q^{-1}:

  \begin{pmatrix} h & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & -h \end{pmatrix}
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} h \cdot 0 + 1 \cdot 1 & h \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot (-h) \\
  1 \cdot 0 + 0 \cdot 1 & 1 \cdot 1 + 0 \cdot (-h) \end{pmatrix}
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.

The (0,1) entry vanishes: h + (-h) = 0. The reverse product T_{nn} \cdot T_{pp} is identical by the same computation.

This is the transfer matrix expression of the Hecke relation: T_{pp} encodes \sigma (crossing coefficient d = 0) and T_{nn} encodes \sigma^{-1} (coefficient d = -h), so T_{pp} \cdot T_{nn} = \sigma \cdot \sigma^{-1} = \mathbf{1}.

(ii) Direct multiplication:

  \begin{pmatrix} h/2 & 1 \\ 1 & -h/2 \end{pmatrix}^2
  =
  \begin{pmatrix} h^2/4 + 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 + h^2/4 \end{pmatrix}.

The diagonal entries are (h/2)(h/2) + 1 \cdot 1 = h^2/4 + 1, and the off-diagonals vanish: (h/2)(1) + 1(-h/2) = 0. Then

  1 + \frac{h^2}{4}
  = 1 + \frac{(q - q^{-1})^2}{4}
  = \frac{4 + q^2 - 2 + q^{-2}}{4}
  = \frac{(q + q^{-1})^2}{4}
  = \frac{[2]_q^2}{4}. \qquad\square
prop:ground-state-ordering:
Proposition The interleaved ordering does not minimise the dilogarithm volume. Let Z protons and N neutrons (A = Z + N) be arranged along the transfer-matrix chain, and let

  \Phi_q = \sum_i \log|\hat{V}_i|

be the quantum dilogarithm volume of that chain. Consider the interleaved, tail-packed arrangement

  \mathrm{ordering}[k]
  =
  \begin{cases}
    1 \text{ (proton)} & k \text{ odd}, \; k < 2Z \\
    0 \text{ (neutron)} & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}

This arrangement does not minimise \Phi_q. Explicitly, at A = 5, Z = 1, N = 4 it is the strict maximiser: the sorted arrangement p\,n\,n\,n\,n satisfies

  \Phi_q(p\,n\,n\,n\,n) < \Phi_q(n\,p\,n\,n\,n)

for every q in an interval containing the aether anchor q_0 \approx 1.10998 and for every Markov parameter lying strictly between the two transfer-matrix eigenvalues, with equality only in the undeformed limit q \to 1.

The eigenvalue relation \lambda_+\lambda_- = -1 for the transfer matrix survives; the ordering claim does not.

Status of the three rules

The proposition previously asserted three rules. An exhaustive sweep of \Phi_q over every \binom{A}{Z} arrangement for A \leq 16, at the experimental (proton) anchor, settles each of them.

(i) Interleaving — refuted for A \geq 4. The interleaved arrangement is the \Phi_q minimiser in 17 of 62 swept cases on the bare-nucleon readout (10 of 62 with the electron tail), and is the strict maximiser in 12 (respectively 8). It is not the ground state.

(ii) Tail packing — refuted. The minimising arrangement head-packs, not tail-packs. At Z = 1 the minimising proton position is A - 5 for every 6 \leq N \leq 15, leaving exactly four neutrons after it and all remaining neutrons before it. For Z \geq 2 the minimiser is an interleaved block at an interior offset with neutron runs on both sides.

(iii) Boundary correction (A \leq 3) — holds at A = 3, fails as stated at A = 2. At A = 3 the sorted arrangement is the exhaustive minimiser, on both readouts and on both sides of Z \leq N. At A = 2 the two arrangements are exactly degenerate on the bare chain — a consequence of the transfer factors commuting, so that the readout sees the crossing coefficients only as a multiset — so sorted does not beat interleaving; and with the electron tail appended, sorted is strictly the worse of the two.

Two readouts, not one

\Phi_q is computed in two inequivalent ways in the corpus: over the bare nucleon chain, and over the nucleon chain with an electron tail appended. The verdicts above are stated for both. They differ only for rule (iii) at A = 2, a case that the production path special-cases and never routes through the ordering at all.

The readout as a two-parameter object

Each transfer factor is T(d) = S + d\,\mathbf{1} for a single fixed matrix S with \mathrm{tr}\, S = q - q^{-1} and \det S = -1. All such factors commute, so the chain product depends on the crossing coefficients only as a multiset, and S^2 = (q-q^{-1})S + \mathbf{1} collapses the product to \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta S. The vertex volume is therefore

  \hat{V}_i = c_+\mu_+ + c_-\mu_-,
  \qquad
  \mu_\pm = \prod_{j > i}(\lambda_\pm + d_{ij}),

with \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} the roots of the characteristic polynomial and, writing z for the Markov parameter,

  c_+ = \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_- = \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_+ + c_- = 1 .

The sum is 1 identically in z, and z enters the readout nowhere else.

Independence of the Markov-parameter convention

The two arrangements differ at positions 0 and 1 only, and that comparison collapses to a single identity in which z survives only inside the product c_+c_-:

  \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(n\,p\,n\,n\,n) - \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(p\,n\,n\,n\,n)
  = 2\,c_+c_-\left(\frac{q + q^{-1}}{2}\right)^{4}\frac{q^6 - 1}{q^3},
  \qquad
  4\,c_+c_- = \frac{4q\,(q - z)(qz + 1)}{(q^2 + 1)^2},

the fourth power being the mixed proton–neutron eigenfactor, which carries no z. For q > 1 every other factor is positive, so the counterexample holds exactly when -q^{-1} < z < q — the Markov parameter strictly between the two eigenvalues. The canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) lies in that window for every q > 1 (since -q^{-1} < 0 < q^3/(q^2+1) < q), so the refutation is a fact about the readout across the entire admissible interval (-q^{-1}, q) rather than an artefact of a particular parameter choice; it degenerates to equality only at q = 1, where the deformation switches off, which is why it holds on a whole interval rather than at a single anchor.

Scope

The A \geq 4 refutation is a structural exclusion: an explicit arrangement with strictly smaller \Phi_q, proved for an interval of q containing the anchor and for every Markov parameter in the window above. The description of the actual minimising family is empirical, covering A \leq 16 only, and no claim is made beyond that range. Which ordering the mass and binding computations should use is a separate question and is not settled here.

rem:ground-state-ordering-derivation:
Remark Ground-state ordering: eigenvalue derivation and verification.

Ground-state ordering: the eigenvalue heuristic and what the sweep found

This remark records the eigenvalue argument that originally motivated the interleaving rule, and the exhaustive search that refuted it.

Transfer matrix eigenvalues

The three transfer matrices (transfer matrix) have eigenvalues determined by the typed crossing operators (typed crossings):

See Table 1.

where h = q - q^{-1}.

Key symmetry: T_{nn} is the q \leftrightarrow q^{-1} mirror of T_{pp}. Their eigenvalues are swapped: \lambda_\pm(T_{nn}) = \lambda_\mp(T_{pp}). The mixed matrix T_{pn} has zero trace and equal-magnitude eigenvalues \pm\sqrt{1 + h^2/4} \approx \pm 1.005.

The heuristic

Each T_{pp} contributes dominant eigenvalue +q \approx 1.110 (growth). Each T_{nn} contributes +q^{-1} \approx 0.901 (decay). The interleaved arrangement alternates growth and decay factors, which suggests destructive interference driving |\hat{V}_i| below 1 at most generators, whereas a sorted chain front-loads pure growth. Since T_{pn} has zero trace, its contributions were expected to average to zero over many chain steps, making the mixed crossings neutral spacers between the binding T_{nn} and anti-binding T_{pp} contributions.

The exhaustive sweep below refutes this heuristic.

What the exhaustive sweep found

\Phi_q was evaluated over every \binom{A}{Z} arrangement for each (Z, N) with Z \leq N and A \leq 16, at the experimental aether anchor, on both the bare-nucleon chain and the chain with the electron tail appended.

The interleaved, tail-packed arrangement is the minimiser in a minority of cases and the strict maximiser in a comparable number. At A = 5, Z = 1 it is the strict worst of all five arrangements on both readouts, while the sorted arrangement — which the rule reserves for A \leq 3 — is the minimiser. The excess neutrons of the minimising arrangement head-pack rather than tail-pack. Full tallies and the proved counterexample are in the proposition.

Why the heuristic failed

The transfer factors are T(d) = S + d\,\mathbf{1} for a single fixed matrix S, so they all commute: the chain product at a position depends on the crossing coefficients only as a multiset, and there is no "alternation" for the readout to see. What looks like a growth/decay interference pattern at the level of individual matrices is, at the level of the readout, a product of eigenfactors whose ordering is immaterial. The only thing that varies between arrangements is which multiset sits at which position — and the resulting \Phi_q is not extremised by alternation.

This also explains an exact degeneracy the heuristic cannot account for: at A = 3, Z = 2 the arrangements ppn and pnp have identical \Phi_q on the bare chain.

Connection to the Gram matrix

The transfer matrix eigenvalues are the Gram matrix entries in disguise: \lambda_+(T_{pp}) = q and \lambda_+(T_{nn}) = q^{-1} are the braiding eigenvalues from the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0. That identification is unaffected by the refutation; only the claim that a particular arrangement extremises \Phi_q does not apply.

Scalability

For A > 16 exhaustive search over \binom{A}{Z} arrangements was not attempted, and no closed-form rule for the minimiser is available. The sweep's minimising family — an interleaved block at an interior offset, with the excess neutrons split between a head run and a four-neutron tail — is an empirical description over A \leq 16, not a derived construction.
prop:skein-generation:
Proposition The skein module of the 3-sphere is free on the unknot. Let R = \mathbb{Q}(a, q) and let \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) be the skein module of oriented links in S^3 over R: the R-module spanned by isotopy classes of oriented links, modulo the HOMFLYPT skein relation

  a\, L_+ - a^{-1} L_- = (q - q^{-1})\, L_0

for every triple (L_+, L_-, L_0) of links that differ only at one crossing. Then \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) is free of rank one, spanned by the unknot U:

  [L] = P_L(a, q)\,[U]

for every oriented link L, where P_L \in R is the HOMFLYPT polynomial normalised by P_U = 1. In particular every link, and so every hadron configuration of rem:hadron-operations, has a terminal skein resolution: a finite reduction of L to a multiple of U.

The specialisation a = 1 is the relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0 of the corpus's Hecke–skein convention, and P_L is then the Conway polynomial in z = q - q^{-1}. At a = q every P_L equals 1, so that specialisation carries no information about L. The reading of this resolution in terms of torus knots, the Hopf link and hadron masses is in rem:skein-generation-hadron-reading.
prf:skein-generation:
Proof Proof of Skein generation. Spanning. Fix a diagram of L with base points on each component and order the crossings. Changing a crossing replaces L_\pm by L_\mp at the cost of a multiple of L_0, which has one fewer crossing; after finitely many changes the diagram is a stack of unknotted, unlinked components (a descending diagram), which is an unlink. Induction on the number of crossings, then on the number of crossings that must be changed, writes [L] as an R-combination of unlinks. For the unlink of c components, apply the relation to a one-crossing kink of one component: L_+ = L_- = the unlink of c components and L_0 is the unlink of c + 1 components, so (a - a^{-1})\,[U^{\sqcup c}] = (q - q^{-1})\,[U^{\sqcup (c+1)}], hence [U^{\sqcup (c+1)}] = \tfrac{a - a^{-1}}{q - q^{-1}}\,[U^{\sqcup c}] in R. So [U] spans.

Freeness. The HOMFLYPT polynomial exists as an isotopy invariant satisfying the relation with P_U = 1 [lickorish1997], so [L] \mapsto P_L is a well-defined R-linear map \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) \to R sending [U] to 1. Hence [U] is not torsion and \mathrm{Sk}(S^3) = R\,[U] is free of rank one, with [L] = P_L [U]. \square
lem:skein-mass-from-linking:

rem:skein-generation-hadron-reading:
Remark Fundamental knots, the Hopf link and the hadron reading of skein generation. In the particle dictionary, a knot type is fundamental if it is the unknot or a torus knot: the unknot (neutrino), the trefoil 3_1, the cinquefoil 5_1 (tau) and the torus (p, 2) family. The electron is not among them: it is \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link, with the trefoil \sigma_0^3 \in B_2 kept as a backup candidate. Every fundamental knot has \mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0, but not conversely: satellite knots, including composites such as 3_1 \# 3_1, also have volume zero. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} is read as the binding operation, and a hadron H \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} as a configuration of fundamental knots joined by Hopf links.

prop:skein-generation resolves every such H to P_H(a, q)\,[U]. In particular the fundamental knots and the Hopf link generate the skein module, but so does the unknot alone, and the resolution records linking only through the polynomial P_H.

The mass reading takes the form \mathfrak{m}(H) = Q(q)\, \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathrm{Vol}(K_i)/\hbar_q^2 of lem:skein-mass-from-linking, so that a hadron built from fundamental constituents takes its whole mass from linking. That step needs a specialisation in which the Hopf link is not identified with the unknot. The specialization a = q, where the skein relation reads q L_+ - q^{-1} L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0, forces P_L = 1 for every link and identifies the Hopf link with the unknot, so it does not supply that step. At a = 1 the Hopf link resolves to (q - q^{-1})\,[U] with the orientation for which its crossings are positive, and the split unlink to 0, so linking is visible there. Which specialisation the mass reading uses is not fixed by the proposition.

lem:pair-skein-mass-formula:
Lemma Pair Skein mass and crossing-by-crossing recursion. The Borromean braid of a nucleon with quarks (q_1, q_2, q_3) contributes a pair Skein mass at each pair of strands. Each pair meets at one positive crossing \sigma and one negative crossing \sigma^{-1}, and the pair Skein mass is the Markov trace of the weighted crossing element at the canonical Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1):

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(\mu_a\,\sigma + \mu_b\,\sigma^{-1}\right)
  =
  \frac{q^{3}\mu_a + q^{-1}\mu_b}
       {q^{2} + 1}.

The total nucleon mass is:

  m_N
  =
  \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_2}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_3}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_2 q_3}(q).

At q = 1 the pair Skein mass is the mean (\mu_a + \mu_b)/2. Exchanging the two species gives \mathcal{S}_{ab} - \mathcal{S}_{ba} = (q - q^{-1})(\mu_a - \mu_b), the Skein coefficient.
prf:pair-skein-mass-formula:
Proof Proof of the pair Skein mass formula. Work in the rank-two Hecke algebra H_2(q) = \mathrm{span}\{1, \sigma\}, where \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1 with h = q - q^{-1}. The inverse crossing is \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h, since \sigma(\sigma - h) = 1. The Markov trace on H_2(q) is \mathrm{tr}_M(a + b\,\sigma) = a + z\,b, and we take z = q^3/(q^2+1).

The Borromean braid of a nucleon with quarks (q_1, q_2, q_3) has six crossings organised into three pairs of strands. Each pair crosses once positively and once negatively, so its linking number is zero. Weight the positive crossing by the dressed quark Skein mass \mu_a of the first strand and the negative crossing by \mu_b of the second. Here \mu_a is the mass contribution of a single quark strand including its strong-field dressing from the Hopf-link interaction with the color background. The pair Skein mass is the Markov trace of the weighted crossing element:

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q)
  = \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(\mu_a\,\sigma + \mu_b\,\sigma^{-1}\right)
  = \mu_a\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) + \mu_b\,\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma - h)
  = \mu_a\, z + \mu_b\,(z - h).

Now z = q^3/(q^2+1) and

  z - h = \frac{q^3}{q^2+1} - q + q^{-1} = \frac{q^{-1}}{q^2+1},

so

  \mathcal{S}_{ab}(q) = \frac{q^{3}\mu_a + q^{-1}\mu_b}{q^{2} + 1}.

At q = 1 this is (\mu_a + \mu_b)/2. The difference \mathcal{S}_{ab} - \mathcal{S}_{ba} = (q^3 - q^{-1})(\mu_a - \mu_b)/(q^2+1) = (q - q^{-1})(\mu_a - \mu_b), since q^3 - q^{-1} = (q - q^{-1})(q^2+1). The total nucleon mass is the sum over the three pairs of strands:

  m_N
  =
  \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_2}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_1 q_3}(q)
  + \mathcal{S}_{q_2 q_3}(q).

\square
prop:flavor-split-aether:
Proposition Closed and factored forms of the aether flavor split. For every nonzero q,

  \frac{(q - 1)^2 \, (1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q}{3},

where \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, h_q = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.
prf:flavor-split-aether:
Proof Proof of the aether-pure flavor split formula. Step 5 proves the identity: dividing (4) by 3 gives it, and it holds for every nonzero q. Steps 1 to 4 and 6 relate its two sides to (m_n - m_p)/M_N under the pair-Skein formula and the ansatz of Step 2, and Step 3 records that the ansatz does not reach them. Those steps are not needed for the identity.

Step 1 (Pair-Skein difference, exact).

Apply Pair Skein mass and crossing-by-crossing recursion to the Borromean baryon braids of the proton (\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) and neutron (\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}). This gives the exact relation:

  m_n - m_p
  \;=\;
  \kappa \cdot (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}),
  \qquad
  \kappa = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma + \sigma^{-1}) = \frac{q^4 + 1}{q\,(q^2 + 1)},

with the Markov trace at the canonical parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). Dividing by \mu_{\text{avg}} = (\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + \mu_{\mathfrak{d}})/2:

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  \kappa \cdot
  \frac{\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}. \tag{1}

Step 2 (Aether ansatz for the per-quark split).

The aether prescription for (\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}})/\mu_{\text{avg}} is:

  \frac{\mu_{\mathfrak{d}} - \mu_{\mathfrak{u}}}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;\approx\;
  h_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{\sqrt{q}},
  \qquad
  h_q = q - q^{-1},
  \quad
  \hbar_q = \frac{q - 1}{q}. \tag{2}

This is the minimal aether-atom combination satisfying three conditions: (a) Bar-involution antisymmetry under q \mapsto q^{-1} (consistent with the antisymmetry of the splitting under flavor exchange \mathfrak{u} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{d}). (b) Leading order (q-1)^3 at the classical limit. (c) Numerical agreement to -0.13\% at the proton-anchored q = q_0.

Scope of Step 2. Equation (2) is a phenomenological ansatz rather than a derived identity: Condition (c) chooses the form because it agrees with experiment, which is selection against the target. Conditions (a) and (b) do not single it out:

  • (b) holds: the right-hand side is 4(q-1)^3 + O((q-1)^4).
  • (a) does not hold as stated. Writing f(q) = h_q^2\,\hbar_q/\sqrt{q}, one finds f(q^{-1}) = -q^2 f(q), so f is antisymmetric under q \mapsto q^{-1} only up to the factor q^2 (checked symbolically).

Everything downstream of (2) therefore inherits a fitted input, and no derivation is on record. One class of derived objects is excluded. Suppose the nucleon masses are additive over strands, m_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2\mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} and m_{\mathfrak{n}} = \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} + 2\mu_{\mathfrak{d}}, and that m_{\mathfrak{p}}/m_{\mathfrak{n}} is a nonzero integer power of q, as for the pivot ratio q^{\pm 2} that the restricted quantum trace gives on the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) commutant. Then, with t = \sqrt{q}, the per-quark split is c\,(t^m - 1)/(t^m + 1) for a nonzero rational c and an integer m \ge 1. This vanishes to first order at q = 1, while the right-hand side of (2) vanishes to third order, so the two never agree, and the ansatz also fails bar-parity symmetry. The exclusion says nothing about non-additive strand rules or about objects that break U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) symmetry.

Step 3 (The ansatz does not reach the closed form).

Substituting (2) into (1) gives

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  \kappa \cdot h_q^2 \cdot \frac{\hbar_q}{\sqrt{q}} .

This is not the closed form \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q of (3) below. At q_0 the ratio of the two is 1.0122. The ansatz (2) was chosen under the retired pair-Skein denominator q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}, for which h_q/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}) = \hbar_q\sqrt{q} made the product collapse to (3). With the derived pair-Skein formula that collapse does not happen, so this sketch no longer supports the conjecture. The conjecture rests on the identity of Step 5 and on the CODATA comparison.

Step 4 (The closed form, as conjectured).

The conjectured per-quark form of the nucleon split is

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{\mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q. \tag{3}

Step 5 (Closed-form polynomial identity).

Substituting \hbar_q = (q-1)/q, h_q = (q^2-1)/q, and [2]_q = (q^2+1)/q into (3):

  \hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^2} \cdot \frac{q^2 - 1}{q} \cdot \frac{q^2 + 1}{q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (q^2 - 1)(q^2 + 1)}{q^4}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (q^4 - 1)}{q^4}
  \;=\;
  (q-1)^2 \cdot (1 - q^{-4}). \tag{4}

Step 6 (Conversion to per-nucleon form).

The per-quark mass averages to the per-nucleon mass via M_N = 3 \mu_{\text{avg}} (one quark mass per strand of the baryon braid, summed over three strands). Therefore:

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{M_N}
  \;=\;
  \frac{m_n - m_p}{3 \mu_{\text{avg}}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h_q \cdot [2]_q}{3}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q-1)^2 \, (1 - q^{-4})}{3}. \tag{5}
